annotations.title: Cut an opening in a plate

description:
Cut a hole (stairwell, duct, riser) in an existing PlateSurface: creates the hole's boundary nodes and appends a PlateOpening to that surface's `openings`. The hole ring must be coplanar with, and lie strictly inside, the outer boundary; elements whose centroid falls in the hole are dropped, so the applied load drops with the removed area (verified: a 1x1 m hole in a 4x4 m slab under 10 kPa took the total reaction from 160000 N to exactly 150000 N).

HARD CONSTRAINT: openings only work with the Delaunay mesher. The structured mesher rejects them outright ("PlateSurface N Structured meshing does not support openings."), so this tool switches the surface to mesh method "Unstructured" with a target_size and tells you it did. That makes the surface's edge-node positions unpredictable, which is why the tool REFUSES to convert a surface whose structured edge grid is carrying a support: those pre-created edge nodes would be stranded off the new mesh and the plate would silently fall back to hanging on its corners (measured 6x too flexible, with the load still balancing exactly). If you need both an opening and a supported edge, author the surface as unstructured from the start and support it by other means.

TARGET SIZE IS A WHOLE-SURFACE SETTING, so a SMALL hole is the expensive case, not the cheap one: left to default (half the shortest hole edge) a 200 mm duct in a 6 m x 6 m slab asks for ~6100 mesh nodes and the engine aborts on that with a raw wasm trap. The default is therefore clamped to what the node budget allows — which means the hole is resolved coarsely and its stress concentration is NOT converged; model the region around the opening as its own smaller surface if you need it sharp. An explicit target_size that busts the budget is refused rather than clamped.

boundary_node_ids.description: Existing node ids bounding the hole instead.

corner_points.description: JSON array of [x,y,z] points bounding the hole, inside the surface and in its plane.

model_ref.description: Handle from stash_model, used INSTEAD of `model`. Avoids sending the whole document on every step; the tool returns the same handle back.

surface_id.description: id of the plate surface to cut the hole in.

target_size.description: Mesh size around the hole, metres. Openings force the Delaunay mesher.
